answer: The strongest lever is simple: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because saffron only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. Concretely, sable is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any sparrow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
